title: Bramble Hill RMS integration — raw call brain dump
body:
High-level: raw capture from discovery call with Bramble Hill (RMS) — getting this into a single place before I forget details. Goal for customer: replace an aging rule-based routing layer with a cheap LLM-assisted ranking and intent routing pipeline. They want tight latency (p95 < 120ms for routing decision) and strict data residency (EU), prefer Private deployment but open to Dedicated if timing/ops simpler.

Attendees (call):
- Bramble Hill: Clare Alden (CTO), Miguel Santos (Platform lead), Ellen Park (sec/infra)
- Redwood: Aisha Kumar (SE, notes), Tom Reynolds (solutions eng)

What they said / context:
- Core product: RMS is an insurance broker routing engine (real-time matching to underwriters). Decisions per request are small JSON payloads + short claims text (avg 400 chars), sometimes up to 2KB.
- Traffic shape: steady 70 RPS baseline, spikes to ~450 RPS during batch windows and mornings; peak burst tolerances required.
- Latency tolerance: p95 target 120ms end-to-end for routing decision (call latency budget ~50ms for inference).
- Residency/compliance: EU-only data; customer must manage keys. They require HSM/KMS integration, audit logs retained 1 year.
- Auth: SAML2 SSO for console access; API access via mTLS for private connect + token rotation.
- Throughput: want autoscaleable capacity but predictability for SLAs; open to reserved capacity for peak windows.
- Model: want a small reranker model (open weights acceptable) + embeddings for dedup/similarity; prefer quantized to save cost but unwilling to accept >2% drop in ranking accuracy.

Requirements (explicit):
1) Private VPC deployment (tenant-managed VPC peering or private link) in eu-west-1.
2) mTLS endpoint with client certs; no public internet egress for payloads.
3) KMS integration with customer's AWS KMS + option for HSM-backed keys for high-value accounts.
4) Audit logs to S3 (encrypted) and shipped to their SIEM; 1y retention.
5) Can pin model versions and roll back quickly; want canary + A/B routing.
6) Latency SLO per model route with alerting integrated to PagerDuty.
7) Cost report per-customer/token-level breakdown in Console.
8) Support for streaming outputs (they may want partial ranking while collecting telemetry).

Gotchas / engineering risks I captured:
- Their runtime is heavily TCP-optimized; any extra network hop (proxying inside their VPC) adds ~7–12ms. Need microbenchmarks with private path.
- Long context cases: some claims include images (they plan to surface OCR text) — text length can exceed 8k tokens occasionally; need to confirm truncation vs fallback policy.
- Embedding sync: they store an index in their DB and want periodic upserts from Redwood embeddings; need clear contract for vector dimensionality and quantization differences.
- Auth: mTLS handshake cost + cert rotation cadence unknown — Ops will need automation (we should propose cert-rotation playbook).
- KMS: they asked for key-wrapping at rest and in transit; need to verify if our Private deployment supports customer-managed keys for model cache and intermediate artifacts.
- Canary traffic shaping: their existing infra expects sticky routing; if our canary changes routing semantics we could bias traffic — request we provide explicit sticky session handling or adapter layer.
- Retries: they have a synchronous pipeline that retries on 5xx; we need idempotency or guidance to avoid double-charging token usage and double inference.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Propose a hybrid: private control plane in Redwood, data plane in their VPC (sidecar workers) to reduce hops and meet residency/KMS requirements.
- Evaluate dedicated reserved pool for peak windows with burst into shared pool as fallback. Model fallback rules for lower-cost variant if capacity constrained; show cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Suggest embedding dimension: start with 1,536 dims (their current FAISS index), propose 1,024 quantized if throughput issues — include eval of recall loss.
- For p95 <120ms target: aim for inference <45ms (model + GPU scheduling), <15ms for network hops, <10ms for pre/post processing — we should run a synthetic test with their sample payloads.

Action items / next steps (owners):
- Aisha: draft architecture diagram (data plane options: sidecar vs private workers) and send to Miguel by 2025-01-20. [JIRA: RMS-413]
- Tom: spin up quick perf POC for routing model (gpt-small-ish reranker quantized) using their sample dataset; target perf numbers and accuracy delta by 2025-01-24. [github PR: rms-proxy-PR-58 reference]
- Ellen (customer): share network diagram, outbound egress policy, and KMS key policy by 2025-01-18.
- Aisha/Tom: prepare cert-rotation automation sketch and mTLS onboarding doc for their infra team by 2025-01-27. [JIRA: OPS-221]
- SE <> Product: price sketch for Reserved Dedicated capacity + Private deployment premium; include retention + audit log add-on by 2025-01-23.

Open questions to resolve on next call:
- Do they require full model weights to remain in-customer environment (on-prem) or is control-plane-managed private deployment acceptable?
- How are embeddings currently encoded (float32 vs float16 vs quantized ints)? need sample vector file.
- Clarify SSO requirements for Console vs API access (console-only SAML or also API-scoped SAML?).
- Confirm SLA expectations for log delivery to their SIEM.

Quick troubleshooting checklist for POC (internal use):
- Validate tokenization delta between our tokenizer and their preprocessor (impact on embedding comparability).
- Measure average token length and distribution from their sample (edge cases >8k).
- Run end-to-end latency microbench with: sidecar -> private worker -> model (quantized) -> return path; capture p50/p95/p99.
- Blackbox test retry loops to ensure idempotency header support (x-request-id).

Misc notes / stream-of-consciousness:
- They seemed anxious about vendor lock-in; emphasize model portability and ability to export serving configs.
- Could pitch Redwood Optimize for embedding dimensionality recommendations + batching tuning.
- Might be a strong case for offering a small on-prem gateway appliance for HSM-key isolation if HSM-in-cloud unacceptable.

End. Save and iterate after engineering triage.

----
Edit log: 2025-01-12 quick update after follow-up email from Miguel — he confirmed their FAISS index is 1536 dims and they can export a 10k sample; added to linked_artifacts and action items above.
